item.description: image1928×2222 549 KB Cheers everyone! We’re hosting another AMA! item.title: CellScript 0.30: Abstractions, Bytes, and the Cost (1 posts)
item.description: Based on branch 0.30, commit 6d75a6e7. The matched cost tests and growth measurements were rerun on September 21, 2026. Version 0.30.0 is for now a release candidate; 0.25 remains the previous stable release. I deliberately put off the byte and execution costs of CellScript’s abstractions until 0.30. Earlier work concentrated on resource lifecycles, successor relations, bounded inputs and outputs, and transactions involving several Scripts. I wanted those abstractions to have a concrete executable meaning first. Cost optimisation came later because I chose that order. That decision now needs a bit of accounting. item.title: How a Fiber Payment Can Unlock Data and Control Settlement (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, I’m Sonny. In my earlier “Chat-and-Pay” and “Charge-as-You-Go” experiments, I focused on one question: can payments happen alongside a service, instead of asking users to top up first, consume later, and wait for a platform to settle everything afterward? While working with Fiber Network 0.9.0, I noticed another useful part of Invoice payments: After an Invoice payment succeeds, the payer can retrieve its payment preimage, exposed as payment_preimage. “Preimage” is a crypto term, but the basic idea is simple: it is a random value generated when the order is created. Fiber calculates a payment_hash from that value. You can think of the hash as its digital fingerprint: Random...
